gestalts.sense: liquid coating applied to a surface
roller frame and cover for applying paint
uniform opacity with no substrate or holidays showing
surface of fastener or part even with the surrounding surface
condition that must hold before work proceeds

loops.name: Load a brush
loops.objective: Carry a working load of paint on the brush without drips.
loops.initial_test: Look at the bristles: dry, or how far paint has been drawn up.
loops.exit_predicate: Bristles are loaded one-third to one-half their length and no drop falls when the brush is held level for a moment.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the bristles: dry, or how far paint has been drawn up.
Compare with the felt memory of a correctly loaded brush for this surface.
Intend to dip only the bristle tips.
Dip bristles one-third to one-half into the paint.
Check the dip depth did not reach the ferrule.
Tap the brush against the inside of the can on both sides; do not wipe on the rim.
Hold the brush level over the can; feel the weight and watch for a forming drop.
Wipe paint off the ferrule and upper bristles with a rag.
Look: ferrule clean, paint only on the lower bristles.
Bristles are loaded one-third to one-half their length and no drop falls when the brush is held level for a moment.

loops.name: Cut in a wall-to-ceiling line
loops.objective: Paint a straight wall edge at the ceiling without touching the ceiling.
loops.initial_test: Look along the next arm's-length of wall-ceiling corner: unpainted wall band remaining?
loops.exit_predicate: A 2-3 inch band is painted along the whole run, the line is straight to the eye, and the ceiling shows no paint.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look along the next arm's-length of the corner for unpainted wall band.
Compare the run against the image of a finished straight band.
Load the brush (see trade.painting.load_brush).
Feel a working load with no drop forming.
Picture the stroke path about a quarter inch below the corner.
Intend one stroke: place the paint off the line, then drag it up to the line.
Press the brush flat to fan the bristles and pull along the line with a steady wrist.
Sight down the fresh edge: straight, and no paint on the ceiling?
Look for a solid band with no holidays.
Wipe the ceiling mark immediately with a damp rag wrapped on a putty knife.
Look: ceiling mark gone.
A 2-3 inch band is painted along the whole run, the line is straight to the eye, and the ceiling shows no paint.

loops.name: Cut in along trim
loops.objective: Paint the wall edge against casing or baseboard without getting wall color on the trim.
loops.initial_test: Look at the wall-trim joint for unpainted wall.
loops.exit_predicate: The wall is painted up to the trim along the whole run with no wall color on the trim face.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the wall-trim joint for unpainted wall.
Compare against a clean painted joint.
Load the brush lightly; trim edges need less paint than open wall.
Feel a light load with no drop.
Intend to lead with the long bristle edge toward the trim.
Draw the brush along the joint, bristle tips just kissing the corner.
Look at the trim face: any wall color on it?
Look for solid wall coverage to the joint.
Wipe the trim mark at once with a damp rag.
Look: trim face clean.
The wall is painted up to the trim along the whole run with no wall color on the trim face.

loops.name: Load a roller
loops.objective: Charge the roller cover evenly without dripping.
loops.initial_test: Look at the roller cover: dry, patchy, or evenly wet all around.
loops.exit_predicate: The cover is evenly wet around its full circumference and does not drip when lifted.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the cover: dry, patchy, or evenly wet all around.
Compare with an evenly charged cover.
Roll into the shallow end of the paint well; do not submerge the frame.
Check paint did not reach the frame ends.
Roll back and forth on the tray ramp or grid several times to spread the load.
Lift the roller; feel for even weight and watch for drips.
The cover is evenly wet around its full circumference and does not drip when lifted.

loops.name: Roll a wall section
loops.objective: Apply an even coat to a roughly 3x4 ft section of wall.
loops.initial_test: Look at the section: bare, partly covered, or evenly coated.
loops.exit_predicate: The section is evenly coated with no holidays, roller marks, or thick edges, blended into the wet edge.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the section: bare, partly covered, or evenly coated.
Compare against the uniform sheen of a finished section.
Load the roller (see trade.painting.load_roller).
Feel an evenly charged roller.
Picture a W or M pattern across the section.
Intend to lay the paint on in the pattern, then fill in without lifting.
Roll the W pattern with light pressure, then fill in the gaps.
Look for gaps or thin spots in the section.
Back-roll top to bottom in one direction with a lightly loaded roller, overlapping each pass.
Look at the section at an angle: even sheen, no ridges, blended into the wet edge?
The section is evenly coated with no holidays, roller marks, or thick edges, blended into the wet edge.

loops.name: Inspect for holidays
loops.objective: Find missed spots and thin areas before paint sets.
loops.initial_test: Look at the painted area head-on.
loops.exit_predicate: Seen at a low angle with a light, the whole area shows uniform color and sheen with no substrate showing.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the painted area head-on.
Shine a work light across the surface at a low angle and look for sheen changes and shadows.
Compare against uniform color and sheen.
Intend to touch up only the defective spots while the surrounding paint is still wet.
Apply a light touch-up and feather it into the surrounding paint.
Look again under raking light.
Seen at a low angle with a light, the whole area shows uniform color and sheen with no substrate showing.

loops.name: Keep a wet edge
loops.objective: Avoid lap marks by always rolling into still-wet paint.
loops.initial_test: Look at and touch-test the edge of the last painted section.
loops.exit_predicate: The whole wall is complete with no visible lap marks at section boundaries.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the edge of the last section: glossy (wet) or dull (setting)?
Compare progress against the finished wall.
Is the leading edge still glossy?
Roll the next section, starting in the dry area and rolling back into the wet edge.
Look at the joint at an angle for a lap mark.
Stop at the nearest natural break (corner or trim), finishing the panel fully.
Look: the break is at a corner or trim line, not mid-wall.
The whole wall is complete with no visible lap marks at section boundaries.

loops.name: Fix a run or drip
loops.objective: Remove a run so it leaves no mark.
loops.initial_test: Look for runs, sags, or drips on the painted surface.
loops.exit_predicate: No run, sag, or drip bead is visible, and the repaired spot matches the surrounding sheen.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look for runs, sags, or drips on the painted surface.
Compare with a clean surface.
Lightly touch nearby excess: still wet?
Brush the run out upward with a nearly dry brush, feathering into the surrounding paint.
Look at an angle: run gone, sheen even?
Leave it; once fully dry, sand the run flat.
Run a hand over it: flat to the touch?
Spot-paint the sanded area, feathering the edges.
Look at an angle: sheen matches.
No run, sag, or drip bead is visible, and the repaired spot matches the surrounding sheen.

loops.name: Sand between coats
loops.objective: Knock down nibs and raised grain so the next coat lies smooth.
loops.initial_test: Run a hand over the dry first coat.
loops.exit_predicate: The surface feels smooth to a flat hand and is wiped free of dust.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Run a flat hand over the dry coat.
Check the paint is dry: no tackiness, no print from a fingernail.
Compare with a smooth surface.
Sand lightly with fine grit (about 220), following the grain, without cutting through.
Look for cut-through to substrate.
Feel again for nibs.
Wipe off dust with a tack cloth or damp rag.
Look and wipe a fingertip: dust-free?
Stop and wait for the recoat time on the label.
Retest: tack-free and hard.
Spot-prime the cut-through area.
Look: spot is covered.
The surface feels smooth to a flat hand and is wiped free of dust.

loops.name: Fill nail holes
loops.objective: Fill nail holes and dents flush before painting.
loops.initial_test: Look at the wall under raking light for holes and dents.
loops.exit_predicate: Every hole is filled, dry, and sanded flush so that no dimple or ridge shows under raking light.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the wall under raking light for holes and dents.
Compare against a flawless surface.
Press spackle into the hole with a putty knife, then scrape the surface clean with the knife held flat.
Look: hole full, little excess around it.
Let the spackle dry.
Press lightly: firm and not cool to the touch?
Sand flush with fine paper on a block.
Run a fingertip across: flush?
Look under raking light for a dimple (shrinkage).
Every hole is filled, dry, and sanded flush so that no dimple or ridge shows under raking light.

loops.name: Caulk a trim gap
loops.objective: Seal the gap between trim and wall with a clean bead.
loops.initial_test: Look along the trim-wall joint for gaps.
loops.exit_predicate: The joint is filled continuously with a smooth, concave bead and no smears on the wall or trim.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look along the trim-wall joint for gaps.
Compare against a sealed, smooth joint.
Cut the caulk tip at 45 degrees with an opening smaller than the gap.
Look at the tip opening against the gap width.
Squeeze with steady pressure and move the gun at a steady pace, pushing the bead into the joint.
Look for a continuous bead with no skips.
Tool the bead with a wet fingertip in one pass; wipe the finger often.
Look: smooth concave bead, no smears.
Wipe smears with a damp rag.
Look: smears gone.
The joint is filled continuously with a smooth, concave bead and no smears on the wall or trim.

loops.name: Mask an edge with tape
loops.objective: Apply painter's tape to protect a surface edge.
loops.initial_test: Look at the edge to be protected.
loops.exit_predicate: Tape runs straight along the whole edge, fully burnished, with no lifted edges or gaps.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the edge to be protected: clean and dry?
Wipe dust off the surface.
Look: surface clean.
Lay the tape in arm-length runs, aligning its edge exactly to the line.
Sight down the tape: straight on the line?
Burnish the paint-side edge with a putty knife or fingernail.
Look for lifted edges, wrinkles, or gaps at joints.
Peel back and relay that run.
Sight down again.
Tape runs straight along the whole edge, fully burnished, with no lifted edges or gaps.

loops.name: Lay drop cloths
loops.objective: Protect floors and furniture from paint.
loops.initial_test: Look at the work area: what surfaces are exposed below the work?
loops.exit_predicate: Every surface below and beside the work is covered, with overlapping seams and no trip hazards.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at what surfaces are exposed below the work.
Picture the drip zone for the work planned.
Move furniture to the center of the room.
Look: walls clear by about 3 feet.
Lay canvas drops along the walls, overlapping seams by about a foot.
Look for bunched or curled edges that could trip.
Look for exposed floor in the drip zone.
Flatten and tape down curled edges.
Look: edges flat.
Every surface below and beside the work is covered, with overlapping seams and no trip hazards.

loops.name: Stir and box paint
loops.objective: Get uniform color and consistency across cans.
loops.initial_test: Look into the opened can for settled pigment or a liquid layer.
loops.exit_predicate: Paint is uniform in color and consistency from top to bottom, with batches boxed together.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look into the can for settled pigment or a liquid layer.
Stir from the bottom up with a stick for a couple of minutes.
Scrape the bottom with the stick: sludge left?
Lift the stick: color and flow uniform?
Check: more than one can needed for this surface?
Pour all cans into one bucket and mix together.
Look: single uniform batch.
Final look at the paint surface for uniformity.
Paint is uniform in color and consistency from top to bottom, with batches boxed together.

loops.name: Clean a latex brush
loops.objective: Remove all latex paint so the brush keeps its shape.
loops.initial_test: Look at the bristles near the ferrule for paint.
loops.exit_predicate: Rinse water runs clear, no paint shows when bristles are spread at the ferrule, and the brush is shaped and hung to dry.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the bristles near the ferrule for paint.
Scrape excess back into the can with the edge of a putty knife.
Look: bulk paint removed.
Wash in warm soapy water, working the bristles with fingers or a brush comb.
Rinse and watch the water: clear?
Spread the bristles at the ferrule: any paint?
Spin or shake out water, reshape the bristles, and hang or put back in its keeper.
Look: bristles straight and together.
Rinse water runs clear, no paint shows when bristles are spread at the ferrule, and the brush is shaped and hung to dry.

loops.name: Scrape loose paint
loops.objective: Remove all loose and flaking paint before priming.
loops.initial_test: Look at the surface for peeling, flaking, or blistered paint.
loops.exit_predicate: No paint lifts when scraped firmly, and edges of remaining paint are feathered.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Check whether the paint could be pre-1978 lead paint (building age or test kit).
Look at the surface for peeling, flaking, or blistering.
Scrape with a sharp scraper pulled toward you at a low angle, firm pressure.
Scrape the area again: does anything still lift?
Sand the edges of the remaining paint to feather them.
Run a hand across the edges: smooth transition?
Stop dry scraping; switch to lead-safe work practices (RRP) or test before continuing.
Confirm lead-safe setup or a negative test is in place.
No paint lifts when scraped firmly, and edges of remaining paint are feathered.

loops.name: Spot-prime repairs
loops.objective: Seal patches and bare spots so the topcoat does not flash.
loops.initial_test: Look for patches, bare wood, or stains.
loops.exit_predicate: Every patch and bare spot has a dry primer coat extending slightly past its edges.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look for patches, bare wood, or stains.
Compare with a uniformly sealed surface.
Brush primer onto each spot, extending slightly beyond its edges.
Look: every spot covered?
Let the primer dry per the label.
Touch-test: dry?
Every patch and bare spot has a dry primer coat extending slightly past its edges.

loops.name: Paint a panel door
loops.objective: Paint a six-panel door in the order that avoids lap marks.
loops.initial_test: Look at the door: hardware removed and surface prepped?
loops.exit_predicate: The whole door face is evenly coated, brushed out in the direction of each part's grain, with no runs at panel edges.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the door: hardware off, surface clean and sanded?
Picture the order: panel moldings, panels, center stile, rails, outer stiles, edges.
Paint the panel moldings and panels first.
Look at panel corners for pooled paint.
Paint the center stile, then rails, then outer stiles, brushing out along each piece's length.
Look at the whole face at an angle for runs and holidays.
Brush out pooled paint from the corners with a nearly dry brush.
Look: corners clean.
Remove the hardware and scuff-sand the door.
Look: ready.
The whole door face is evenly coated, brushed out in the direction of each part's grain, with no runs at panel edges.

loops.name: Paint baseboard
loops.objective: Paint baseboard without picking up floor dirt or marking the floor or wall.
loops.initial_test: Look along the baseboard: masked and dust-free?
loops.exit_predicate: The baseboard face and top edge are evenly coated with no marks on floor or wall and no picked-up grit.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look along the baseboard: floor masked, dust vacuumed?
Load the brush lightly.
Feel a light load.
Paint the top edge, then the face, in long strokes along the board.
Look for grit or hairs in the wet paint.
Look along the run for coverage.
Pick out grit with the brush tip and brush smooth.
Look: clean.
Vacuum along the board and tape the floor.

loops.name: Test readiness to recoat
loops.objective: Decide when the previous coat can take the next coat.
loops.initial_test: Read the recoat time on the label and note the time the last coat finished.
loops.exit_predicate: The label's recoat time has passed and the coat is tack-free and does not mark under light pressure.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Read the recoat time on the label and the time the last coat finished.
Adjust expectation for humidity and cold, which lengthen drying.
Check the clock: has the recoat time passed?
Touch an inconspicuous spot: tacky, or does a light fingernail leave a mark?
Wait, improving airflow if possible.
Check the clock again.
The label's recoat time has passed and the coat is tack-free and does not mark under light pressure.

loops.name: Clean a roller cover
loops.objective: Clean a latex roller cover for reuse.
loops.initial_test: Look at the nap for paint.
loops.exit_predicate: Water squeezed from the nap runs clear and the cover is stood on end to dry.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the nap for paint.
Scrape paint out with the curved edge of a 5-in-1 tool back into the can.
Look: most paint removed.
Rinse under running water, squeezing the nap repeatedly.
Squeeze and watch: water clear?
Spin out water and stand the cover on end to dry.
Look: standing on end, nap not crushed.
Water squeezed from the nap runs clear and the cover is stood on end to dry.

loops.name: Feather a touch-up
loops.objective: Touch up a spot on a dry wall so it doesn't show.
loops.initial_test: Look at the damaged or dirty spot under normal room light.
loops.exit_predicate: The touched-up spot cannot be picked out from normal viewing distance under normal light.
loops.source_basis: O*NET-SOC 47-2141.00 Painters, Construction and Maintenance; occupation reference only. Steps machine-drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-09-29; not observed or verified.

steps.text: Look at the spot under normal room light.
Picture the smallest patch that covers the defect.
Load a nearly dry brush or small roller with the same paint.
Feel a very light load.
Apply to the spot, then feather outward with lighter strokes.
Look for a thick edge.
Let it dry fully (touch-ups often look different wet).
View from normal distance under normal light: can the spot be picked out?
